newsitem.title: UK: NatWest sees profits tumble at Markets arm.
newsitem.headline: NatWest sees profits tumble at Markets arm.

text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc said on Tuesday first half pre-tax profits at its troubled investment banking arm NatWest Markets were 58 million pounds ($94.5 million), compared with 219 million pounds for the same period in 1996.

But the banking group said its Global Financial Markets (GFM) arm, which was separated from NatWest Markets in a restructuring announced last week, had recorded pre-tax profits for the period of 169 million pounds.

NatWest's chief executive Derek Wanless said not all of NatWest Markets' profits were as volatile as appeared from the sector's results but said the group had recognised its aspirations had to be more focused.

Wanless said the changes resulting from the 77 million pound options mispricing loss would ensure "the business develops in a profitable and controlled manner", adding it was well positioned to offer a full range of investment banking services in Europe.

He was upbeat about the prospects for NatWest as a whole. "The group is committed to delivering value to our shareholders. We are confident that despite the recent setback at NatWest Markets we will do so."

Wanless said Konrad "Chip" Kruger, who was last week named as the replacement for former NatWest Markets chief executive Martin Owen had brought "knowledge, clarity and focus" that would be hugely beneficial to the operation. Owen resigned in the wake of the options scandal, which also saw the departure of a handful of key senior managers.

Last Friday, NatWest announced changes which meant the Markets' division would lose the Treasury, Foreign Exchange and other sections which would form a new part of the group called Global Financial Markets (GFM).

NatWest said the rump, still to be known as NatWest Markets, made a loss of 111 million pounds ($180.9 million) in the first half including the 77 million pounds deduction for the losses on interest rate options, compared to 219 million pounds last year.
NatWest said its main retail and commercial banking operations had performed well but still needed to deliver services more cheaply and make better use of existing relationships.
Post-tax return on equity in the UK business was 25.2 percent but NatWest Markets as was, made a return of just 2.4 percent in the first half.

NatWest said it would not be making major acquisitions and said any surplus capital would be returned to shareholders. Its tier one capital ratio now stands at 6.8 percent, well in the middle of its comfort range.
-- Joe Ortiz, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8864. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
